statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 10 (low) holds well below the block threshold as the overnight Larak Island / Jordan exchange stays absorbed and the 29,274.75 low survives a fifth hour, while Stress 41 (moderate) reflects an uncorroborated Kharg Island claim, crude near $85 and a macro week ending in nonfarm payrolls.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 13:30-14:30 UTC, where the U.S. cash open on the final August session meets month-end rebalancing and the first deep-liquidity pricing of the weekend exchange with Iran. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100: overnight shock stays absorbed as Asia keeps retracing and an unverified Kharg Island claim holds Stress up
body:
The overnight picture is unchanged in direction and slightly better in structure. The Nasdaq-100 September contract trades 29,352.50, down 139.25 points or 0.47% against Friday's 29,491.75 settlement, inside an overnight range of 29,274.75 to 29,545.50. The 29,274.75 low was printed around the 00:00 UTC hour, when Iran's Revolutionary Guards answered Sunday's U.S. strike on two rocket launchers at Larak Island with ballistic missiles and drones against the King Hussein and Al Azraq air bases in Jordan. Jordan's armed forces reported intercepting eight missiles that entered its airspace and said the interception operation was complete. That low has now held for roughly four and a half hours of two-sided trade, and the model's Tail has fallen from a 15 peak to 10 across that span.

Regional cash markets tell the same story. The Nikkei 225 trades 65,812.50, down 0.89%, the Kospi is down 1.40% and the Hang Seng down 0.71%, all substantially recovered from declines that reached 2.4% and 3.6% at the worst of the overnight repricing. Shanghai is down 0.20% and the ASX 200 down 0.17%. That is retracement, not persistent one-way extension, and it is the evidence that keeps Tail low.

The one genuinely new item since the last assessment is a social-media post from President Trump stating that Kharg Island, which handled roughly 90% of Iran's pre-war crude exports, was 'being blown to smithereens'. The post carried a video clip that Reuters, using AI-detection software, assessed as most likely synthetically generated, and neither the White House nor the Defense Department confirmed any strike. Markets have priced it accordingly: WTI trades $85.25, up 2.22%, and Brent $90.27, up 2.46%, firm on the Larak Island strike and the Strait of Hormuz mining threat but nowhere near the levels an actual loss of Kharg would imply. The claim is treated here as an open headline thread that supports Stress rather than as verified escalation that would support Tail.

Cross-asset context is mildly risk-off but orderly. The U.S. 10-year yield is 4.71% and the 2-year 4.33%, both steady after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole address left futures pricing roughly a 57% chance of a 25 basis-point hike on 16 September, up from about 36% before the speech. The VIX last printed 14.43 at Friday's close and cash volatility does not trade in this window, so the volatility read is a Friday reference rather than a live one.

The calendar is empty until the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index at 14:30 UTC, but the week is heavy: ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on Tuesday, ADP on Wednesday, jobless claims and ISM Services on Thursday, and August nonfarm payrolls on Friday. Today is also the final cash session of August, a month the Nasdaq Composite led higher by roughly 4%, so month-end index and pension rebalancing sits on top of the 13:30 UTC open. The London Summer Bank Holiday is expected to thin the European session throughout. Those factors concentrate risk in the narrow 13:30-14:30 UTC window rather than across the whole day, which is where the danger window is placed.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, covering the closed Sunday market, the CME weekly reopen and the first hours of the new session. The first eighteen of those hours sat inside the weekend halt with Tail fixed at the floor of 5, dominant mode normal and status green, while Stress drifted from 26 to 32 as the reopen approached and Confidence rebuilt from 58 to 87 as primary sources were re-verified each hour. The 22:00 UTC reopen lifted Tail to 9, and the Larak Island strike and Iran's reply on the Jordan air bases carried it to a 15 peak at 00:00 UTC with Stress 44 and the only trend-down reading of the window. Every hour since has stepped down, 13 then 11 then 10, as the 29,274.75 low held and Asia retraced, with Confidence steady at 88. Status was green and the mapped action EA_ON in all 24 hours.
outlookSummary: The current hour records an absorbed shock that has not been extended: NQ 29,352.50, down 0.47%, the 29,274.75 low intact roughly four and a half hours, and Asian cash indices well off their worst levels, so Tail holds at 10 with Stress 41 and Confidence 88. The conditional path eases to a trough of 9 across the quiet Asian hours, holds near 9 to 10 through a European session thinned by the London Summer Bank Holiday, then builds through the U.S. pre-market to a conditional peak of 15 in the hour containing the 13:30 UTC cash open, where month-end rebalancing meets the first deep-liquidity pricing of the weekend exchange. It decays through the U.S. afternoon, ticks back to 12 into the month-end closing auction, and settles at 8 to 9 overnight into the 1 September Asian session. Every slot in the published path maps to EA_ON; none reaches the block threshold. The stated invalidation is a break of 29,274.75 followed by repeated extension after failed retracements, or corroboration of an actual strike on Kharg Island.
